title: A positive proportion of integers are sums of three cubes
credit: Folklore density form of the sums-of-three-cubes problem; conditional results by Diaconu (2019) and V. Y. Wang (2021-23)
premise_risks: Conditional 100% result by Wang: check that no 2025-26 unconditional improvement exists beyond what searches found
Scorer may judge as close to the famous full problem; it is a strictly weaker, distinct milestone
plain: An integer a^3+b^3+c^3 (with a, b, c integers, negatives allowed) never leaves remainder 4 or 5 on division by 9, and every other integer is believed to be such a sum. Nobody can even prove that a fixed positive fraction of integers are sums of three cubes. Prove that for some c>0, at least cN of the integers 1, ..., N are sums of three integer cubes for all large N.
math: Let $\mathcal C=\{a^3+b^3+c^3: a,b,c\in\mathbb Z\}$. Prove $\liminf_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\#\{1\le n\le N: n\in\mathcal C\}>0$. (Conjecturally the density exists and equals $7/9$.)
